introduction: The Qur’an calls Muhammad “the Seal of the Prophets”, and Muslims have understood that no messenger can come after him. The Báb and Bahá’u’lláh were condemned on that verse. These readings honour the title and reinterpret it: prophethood, as a stage in which a future Day of God was foretold, did end with Muhammad, and what follows is the Day itself; and since every Manifestation is in essence all of them, “first” and “last” apply to each. Reading 20 observes that Jews and Christians reasoned the same way about Moses and Jesus. The verses they relied on are set beside the Qur’an’s here: “there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses”, “ye shall not add”, “no man cometh unto the Father, but by me”, “the faith once delivered”, the curse on whoever adds to the Apocalypse. Against them stand the texts in each scripture that point forward, “I have yet many things to say unto you” and Malachi’s promise of Elijah.
questions: What does “Seal of the Prophets” mean on the reading given here, and what does it still exclude?
Each scripture has both a closing verse and a forward-looking one. How should a believer weigh the two kinds?
Reading 18 says a verse was used to justify killing. What responsibility do interpreters of scripture bear?
If the Bahá’í Faith also expects a further Manifestation after a thousand years, how does it guard against repeating the pattern it criticizes?

outside.why: “I am all the Prophets … I am Adam, Noah, Moses, and Jesus.” Before Abraham was, I am.
The Qur’an’s own ground for such a saying, in the believers’ creed: we make no distinction between any of His messengers.
Blessings on the Seal of the Prophets, through whom unity was spread. We sent thee not save as a mercy for the peoples.
The verse in question: Muhammad is not the father of any man among you, but he is the messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets.
They argued that the word is explicit and final. The Bible ends on a similar seal: if any man shall add unto these things, God shall add unto him the plagues that are written in this book.
And the Torah has one: ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye diminish ought from it.
He denies having repudiated Muhammad’s prophethood. Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets.
They have not understood the meaning of the Seal. I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now. Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth.
The verse fulfilled in a Day beyond prophethood. I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come.
Every age of a Manifestation is God’s appointed Day. Every nation hath its term.

The prophetic cycle ended with Muhammad. Hebrews says of an earlier ending: God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets, hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son.
The ordinances of the Qur’an, among them the Seal. For everything there is a time prescribed.

The Báb as the promised one of the Qur’an. The last words of the last Hebrew prophet look past himself: behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord.
They clung to a verse and killed Him for claiming prophethood. We know that God spake unto Moses: as for this fellow, we know not from whence he is.
Muslims have followed the same footsteps as those before them. The Jewish form of the claim: there arose not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses.
And the Christian form: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.
The faith which was once delivered unto the saints. Each community has a verse that seems to close the door after its own founder. What do the readings propose as the right way to read all of them?
A homely image for children: a teapot complete in itself, and other vessels after it. Neither do men put new wine into old bottles.

Muslims thought Muhammad greater because of the title. Jesus on the greatest of the old order: among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he. What does “greatest” mean in a sequence of messengers?
